messages:
alex: Hey folks — need approvals for a short-lived spot/preemptible H100 pool in us-central1. Plan: spin up ~20 H100 nodes for nightly batch inference (6h run). Primary asks: increase GPU quota for H100 to 20, and decide networking approach for egress.

alex: Right now we're debating between assigning ephemeral external IPs to each node vs using Cloud NAT with reserved NAT IPs. Pref would be NAT for fewer external IPs, but some of our telemetry requires per-node IPs for IP-based allowlists.

alex: Project: projects/redwood-batch-dev (billing: infra-billing). Target window: Thu 03:00-09:00 UTC next week. Who can open the GCP quota request and approve project-level changes? @riley tagging for billing ok.

riley: I can open the quota ticket. Quick Qs: 1) Are these GCE instances or GKE node pool? 2) Do you need full external IPs (static) or ephemeral primary external IPs (assigned per instance)? Cloud NAT is usually cheaper and simpler for scale.

alex: It's GKE node pool (node pool will be spot/spot-similar). We prefer ephemeral external IPs for per-node allowlist, but could change telemetry to use an egress proxy. For now assume we need 20 ephemeral external IPs (+10 static for control plane).

sam: FYI on GCP, "spot" VMs are preferred over old "preemptible" nomenclature. Quota for accelerators (H100) is separate from CPU/GPU quota; you need to request per accelerator type in the region (us-central1). Expect 24–72h for org approval if it touches org-level limits.

lee: Also check VPC-NAT ephemeral port quotas if you're doing high outbound traffic — Cloud NAT and ephemeral ports can be a bottleneck. If telemetry opens many concurrent connections per node we may need to bump ephemeral port quotas or add multiple NAT IPs.

alex: Good call. Telemetry opens ~150 concurrent outbound connections per node during startup. If we use Cloud NAT we probably need 10 NAT IPs to keep connection saturation low.

maria: Rough cost note: spot H100 pricing fluctuates; put a conservative estimate in the ticket and request a short test window first (2 nodes) to validate runtime and boot behavior. Saves headaches if there's a quota scarcity.

alex: Agreed — will start with a 2-node smoke test then request full 20. Riley — if you can open the ticket, add both the initial test and the full-run request. Include need for: "Accelerator quota: H100 (us-central1) -> 20 units" and "Compute External IP quota -> 30 (20 ephemeral + 10 static)" and "Cloud NAT NAT IPs -> 10 (if choosing NAT path)".

riley: OK I'll open the ticket now. Drafting description and org justification. Will submit to GCP support and cc infra-sre. Ticket will include the gcloud sample and links to node template.

riley: Draft command snippets in the ticket (for reference):
```
# check current regional accelerator quota
gcloud compute regions describe us-central1 --project=redwood-batch-dev --format="yaml(quota)"

# request quota increase via console: https://console.cloud.google.com/iam-admin/quotas
```

infra-bot: ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-3421 — GCP quota request (H100 spot pool + external IPs). Assigned: @riley.

riley: INFRA-3421 created. I put the test step (2 nodes) and roll plan, and set requested timeline for Thu next week. If org approval required we'll escalate to finance for a short-term exception.

alex: Thanks — tagging @lee and @maria to review ticket notes. I'll prepare the smoke test node template and push it to repo infra/gke/node-templates.

lee: Reviewed ticket, added note about NAT port scaling and suggested metrics to validate during smoke test (outbound conn per node, conn saturation, CPU/GPU boot time).

maria: Added cost estimates and fallback plan (reduce to 10 nodes if spot scarcity). Also noted to collect prometheus metrics and post run summary in the ticket.

riley: Will follow up once GCP confirms quota. If we get pre-approval faster we can run the smoke test earlier. :thumbsup:

alex: Great — thanks everyone. Keeping this thread as the canonical log for the request.
